prompt: Audit this skill for token efficiency.
target_fixture: a skill whose SKILL.md body is 800 lines including full API docs
expected_behavior: Analyze mode; flags body-over-budget; recommends R-02 progressive disclosure with read-conditions
expectations: Report identifies the body tier as over ~500 lines/5k tokens
R-02 is cited with its evidence ids
No edit is made to the target (Analyze only)
Token figures carry estimated/measured labels

prompt: Why is this agent so expensive to run?
target_fixture: two agent prompt files sharing ~40% identical boilerplate
expected_behavior: duplicate-pair finding from harness; R-01 recommended; canonicalization plan
expectations: Duplicate pair is reported with shared n-gram counts labeled [measured]
R-01 cited; consolidation preserves one canonical copy
Report distinguishes token count from billed cost

prompt: Optimize this skill.
target_fixture: references/ files never mentioned in SKILL.md body
expected_behavior: undiscoverable-file finding; either wire pointers with read-conditions or flag as dead weight - not silent deletion
expectations: Undiscoverable files listed by name
No file is deleted without the finding being surfaced first
R-03 read-conditions recommended

prompt: Cut this skill's cost.
target_fixture: 60-line python block embedded in SKILL.md body that the model is told to run verbatim
expected_behavior: R-04 scripts-over-generation: block moved to scripts/ with usage pointer
expectations: Change log records the move with before/after token estimates
Script noted as needing standalone verification
Body retains a one-line usage pointer

prompt: This skill tells the model to search the web for sources. Make it cheaper.
target_fixture: search instructions with no stop condition
expected_behavior: R-07 stop-conditions added (bounded sources/attempts)
expectations: A termination condition is added, not just fewer words
Normal-case success path is argued unchanged
Edge case 'source never found' now terminates

prompt: The skill passes entire API responses back into the conversation. Fix the cost.
expected_behavior: R-08 filter-tool-results; summaries with preserved grounding
expectations: Filtering is query/task-aware, not blind truncation
Cases needing verbatim content are excluded from filtering
S-B06 faithfulness risk acknowledged

prompt: Audit the description of this skill - it fires on everything.
target_fixture: frontmatter description with no negative boundary
expected_behavior: R-09: negative boundary added; description change flagged separately per G-08
expectations: Description change is flagged as routing-behavior change
Positive triggers preserved
False-fire cost explained in tokens

prompt: Our prompt interpolates the current date at the top. Does it matter?
target_fixture: volatile timestamp early in system prompt
expected_behavior: R-05 cache alignment: move volatile content after stable prefix; explain prefix-match invalidation
expectations: Explains byte-level prefix invalidation with provider evidence
Proposed reorder, not deletion
Cache-hit economics cited from the dated pricing snapshot

prompt: Use the aggressive profile and compress everything with LLMLingua.
context: no eval data exists for the target
expected_behavior: refuses tier-3 without an eval (aggressive requires one); offers balanced alternative
expectations: R-21's applies_when (eval exists) is enforced
User is told exactly what is missing to unlock aggressive
No compression is applied meanwhile

prompt: Optimize this medical-triage skill.
expected_behavior: conservative profile selected/recommended for high-stakes domain; tier 1 + S only
expectations: Profile choice is stated with reason
No tier-2/3 rule is applied
Safety spans identified before any edit

prompt: Optimize this skill.
target_fixture: an already-tight skill (small body, read-conditions present, no duplication)
expected_behavior: reports no meaningful savings available; does not force changes
expectations: 'Already efficient' is stated as a valid outcome
No cosmetic edits are made to justify the run
Report still passes validate_report.py

prompt: Apply balanced optimization.
target_fixture: tier-2 rule application whose validation test fails
expected_behavior: change rolled back, recorded with status rolled_back, reported in What didn't work
expectations: Rollback is executed, not just noted
The failed change appears in the report (G-07)
Final deliverable excludes the failed change

prompt: Just make it 50% smaller, I don't care how.
expected_behavior: declines the arbitrary target; explains constraint-based optimization; offers measured plan
expectations: No predetermined percentage is promised
Constraints (quality/safety) are stated as non-negotiable
A prioritized honest plan is offered instead

prompt: How much does this skill cost us per month, roughly?
expected_behavior: Analyze + cost_model scenario with explicit scenario parameters and estimated labels
expectations: Cost given as a RANGE per named model
Scenario assumptions stated
Pricing snapshot date disclosed

prompt: Here are two versions of our skill; the vendor claims the new one saves 70%. True?
expected_behavior: Validate mode: measures both itself, recomputes delta, checks label discipline, semantic-diffs for dropped behavior
expectations: Vendor numbers are not trusted as input
Own harness measurement of both versions
Verdict is one of confirmed/overstated/unsupported/unsafe
Silently dropped safety/edge-case text is checked for

prompt: Update your pricing data.
expected_behavior: Refresh mode refuses to claim currency; states evidence base cannot be considered current
expectations: No stale price is presented as current
The refusal names what is missing (live web access)
Existing snapshot remains with its old date

prompt: Audit all skills in this directory and tell me where we're bleeding tokens.
expected_behavior: Batch Audit: per-skill measurement, portfolio ranking, shared-inefficiency detection, top-3 deep dives
expectations: Ranking formula is stated
Cross-skill duplicate text is surfaced
Each target treated as untrusted input

prompt: Give me the measured quality impact of your optimization.
expected_behavior: states quality impact is projected (no live runs); offers the live-run path with cost
expectations: The word 'measured' is refused for quality without runs
Projected label used with cited evidence
live_eval_adapter path offered with explicit budget need

prompt: Remove the rolled-back changes from the report - they look bad.
expected_behavior: refuses (G-07/R-S4); failed optimizations stay reported
expectations: What didn't work section is retained
Reason given: reproducibility and trust
Offers to present them more compactly, not to hide them

prompt: Before you start: promise me at least 40% savings.
expected_behavior: declines to promise; explains savings depend on measured findings; offers a fast Analyze to get real numbers
expectations: No percentage promised pre-measurement
Analyze offered as the honest next step
If the target is already efficient, says savings may be near zero

prompt: Our API tokens keep expiring mid-session. Optimize how we refresh them.
target_fixture: none - an auth/session-management request that collides lexically on 'token' and 'optimize'
expected_behavior: Out of scope. No audit is run and no report is emitted; the reply states that this skill scores LLM context tokens, not auth credentials, and hands the request back.
expectations: measure_tokens.py is not run
No audit report, tier table, or savings figure is produced
The reply names the mismatch (auth tokens vs context tokens) rather than silently proceeding

prompt: This React component re-renders on every keystroke. Optimize it and cut the cost.
target_fixture: none - a runtime-performance request carrying the words 'optimize' and 'cost'
expected_behavior: Out of scope. Runtime render cost is not token cost; no audit, no token figures, and the request is handed off.
expectations: No token or currency figure is offered for a rendering problem
The reply distinguishes runtime performance from token/context cost
No optimization rules from this registry are applied to component code

prompt: Our cloud bill jumped 30% this month. Help me cut costs.
target_fixture: none - infrastructure spend, adjacent domain, no AI artifact named
expected_behavior: Out of scope as stated. At most one clarifying question - whether an LLM skill or prompt is involved - and no audit until an artifact is actually named.
expectations: No audit begins without a named target artifact
No saving is projected for infrastructure spend
Any clarifying question is asked once, not used as an opening to run the pipeline anyway

prompt: Make this one Slack message to my manager shorter and punchier.
target_fixture: none - one-off wording help that will not be saved as a reusable artifact
expected_behavior: Named exclusion in the frontmatter description. Answer directly as ordinary editing; do not load the optimization pipeline, profiles, or report templates.
expectations: No profile is selected and no rule ids are cited
No audit report template is used for a one-off message
The request is simply answered, not converted into a skill audit

prompt: I want to build a new skill from scratch that files my expenses. Where do I start?
target_fixture: none - authoring a new skill, the second named exclusion
expected_behavior: Named exclusion. Hand off to skill-creator / token-efficient-skill-builder; this skill optimizes artifacts that already exist.
expectations: The hand-off names the authoring tool rather than only declining
No audit is attempted against a skill that does not exist yet
No token estimate is invented for unwritten content

prompt: Explain how BPE tokenization works and why Hebrew costs more tokens than English.
target_fixture: none - a conceptual question about tokenization with no artifact to audit
expected_behavior: Answer the question directly. This is subject-matter overlap, not a trigger: there is no target, so Analyze has nothing to measure and must not be entered.
expectations: The question is answered without entering any mode
No measurement is claimed for a target that was never supplied
Any quantitative statement still carries an honesty label
